patch_resolves_note: The staged patch.diff moves `memset(residual, 0, residual_len)` ahead of the parse and removes the old empty-suffix-only clear. The patched-source fixed rebuild in the reused vulnerable workspace failed during the fallback full build for environment reasons, so fixed-side execution used the authoritative `n132/arvo:32482-fix` image. That fixed original still executes the same non-empty residual path and records the residual buffer as fully initialized before and after the partial copy.
verification_limitations: Fixed-side execution used the authoritative `-fix` image after the patched-source full rebuild in the reused workspace failed with `configure: error: cannot run C compiled programs`.

nodes.description: At the `strlen(buffer)` sink inside `lxc_trim_whitespace_in_place()`, the vulnerable execution reads past the initialized one-byte residual prefix into the uninitialized tail of the caller's 3-byte stack buffer.
nodes.evidence: The vulnerable assertion trace records `trim_strlen_sink.buffer_read_bytes=2` and `trim_strlen_sink.buffer_initialized_prefix_len=1` immediately before the crashing `strlen(buffer)` call.

nodes.description: On the non-empty suffix path, `memcpy(residual, remaining, len)` writes only the parsed `.` suffix into the residual buffer and, on the vulnerable execution, leaves the remaining two bytes uninitialized.
nodes.evidence: The vulnerable assertion trace records `residual_partial_copy.residual_initialized_prefix_len=1` and `residual_partial_copy.residual_len=3` immediately after `memcpy(residual, remaining, len)`.

edges.description: The same `residual` buffer whose missing initialization is observed at the root site is the destination buffer consumed by the later partial `memcpy` on the non-empty suffix path.
edges.evidence: The vulnerable assertion trace records `residual_root_state.residual_ptr == residual_partial_copy.residual_ptr`.

edges.description: The partially initialized residual buffer produced by the short `memcpy` is passed unchanged into `lxc_trim_whitespace_in_place()` and becomes the `buffer` argument consumed by the crashing `strlen` sink.
edges.evidence: The vulnerable assertion trace records `residual_partial_copy.residual_ptr == trim_strlen_sink.buffer_ptr`.

root_cause_criterion.missing_conjunct: `residual[0..residual_len)` is initialized before the non-empty suffix path reaches `memcpy(residual, remaining, len)`.
root_cause_criterion.criterion: When `strtoll()` leaves a non-empty suffix, `lxc_safe_int64_residual()` must still zero the full residual buffer before it copies the suffix into caller storage. Otherwise a short suffix copy can leave the tail of the caller's stack buffer uninitialized and later string consumers will scan into poisoned bytes.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable helper reaches the non-empty suffix path with `residual` still entirely uninitialized, because its only `memset(residual, 0, residual_len)` is guarded by `*remaining == '\0'`. The fixed original reaches the same protected partial-copy event with all three bytes of `residual` initialized.
root_cause_criterion.verification_note: The vulnerable original reaches `residual_partial_copy` with `residual_root_state.residual_initialized_prefix_len=0` and `residual_root_state.residual_len=3`, so the required predicate is violated while the protected partial copy executes. The authoritative fixed original reaches the same protected event genuinely with `residual_root_state.residual_initialized_prefix_len=3` and `residual_root_state.residual_len=3`.
